report:
Your view is supported by good, though not conclusive, evidence.

**Strongest evidence:** A systematic review and meta-analysis (Kappelmann, Lewis, Dantzer, Jones & Khandaker, published in Molecular Psychiatry) pooled 20+ randomized controlled trials involving over 5,000 patients with rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, Crohn's disease and other chronic inflammatory conditions who received anti-cytokine drugs (mainly anti-TNF agents, but also IL-6 and IL-12/23 inhibitors). They found a significant reduction in depressive symptoms compared with placebo, with effect sizes in the small-to-moderate range—comparable to those seen with conventional antidepressants (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/). Notably, the improvement in mood was largely independent of improvement in physical disease severity, suggesting a genuine biological (not just secondary/psychological) effect of reducing inflammation on depressive symptoms (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/; summarized in https://pharmaceutical-journal.com/article/news/anti-inflammatory-drugs-could-treat-symptoms-of-depression and https://www.newscientist.com/article/2109382-anti-inflammatory-drugs-can-relieve-symptoms-of-depression/).

**Caveats:** Depressive symptoms were measured as a secondary outcome in most trials (not the primary target), so measurement was sometimes crude. Effect sizes, while statistically significant, were modest. Publication bias and heterogeneity across conditions/drugs are possible. The authors themselves note the antidepressant effect might partly reflect improvement in cytokine-induced "sickness behavior" symptoms (fatigue, anhedonia) rather than core depression, and call for dedicated trials.

**Conclusion:** The claim is reasonably well-supported by meta-analytic RCT data, with a plausible mechanistic pathway (inflammation-depression link) and evidence the effect isn't purely secondary to physical improvement. However, effects are modest, and further targeted trials are needed to confirm causality and clinical significance.
